findings.title: Per-agent spatial query contract contradicts the vectorized hot-path requirement
findings.description:
`SpatialQuery.query_radius(position, radius)` answers for one position, and `BulkForce` receives `neighbor_lists: list[NDArray]`. This forces a Python-level loop over active agents, which conflicts with three stated requirements:
- **Slice's own technical requirement (line 247):** "No Python-level per-agent loops in the hot path."
- **Architecture, Efficient large-scale evaluation:** the hot loop must be "structured for vectorized computation over arrays of agent state."
- **Architecture, GPU compute path:** "bulk array-in/array-out… no dynamic allocation."

Slice 105 must swap "behind the existing query interface" and 101–104 code against `neighbor_lists`, so this shape is locked in here.

Related gaps on the same path:
- **Brute-force description is inconsistent.** It precomputes all pairwise distances in `build()`, but `query_radius` takes an arbitrary position, not an agent index, so the matrix cannot be used.
- **Build cost ignores the subset.** The N×N build is paid in full even when three agents are active.
- **Profile lookups are per-agent.** Radius and `max_speed` come from `list[BehavioralProfile]`, with no stated vectorized gather by `profile_indices`.
- **The NFR is not restated.** The architecture's target is "tens of thousands of agents at full behavioral fidelity on a single CPU process"; the slice only says "hundreds-of-agents scale."

Fix: define a batch query (active indices plus per-agent radii in, flat pair or CSR-style arrays out) and restate the NFR, noting brute-force is exempt from it until 105.

findings.title: BulkForce return shape and integration scope contradict each other
findings.description:
Line 152 says forces return a full-population N×2 array so integration can "add force to velocity for all." Line 215 and data-flow step 5 say integration applies only to `active_indices` via fancy indexing.

These are different designs with different results. Integrating all agents with zero force still advances inactive positions by `velocity * dt`, which violates the criterion "all others are unchanged" (line 241).

The full-population return also allocates N×2 per force per tick regardless of subset size. That undercuts the subset-evaluable tick principle the slice is meant to enable.

Fix: pick one contract. Returning a `len(active)×2` array integrated by fancy index is the lighter option.

findings.title: Per-agent `Force` protocol and `accelerations` array have no consumer
findings.description:
- **`Force` has no path into `tick()`.** The signature accepts only `list[BulkForce]`, yet line 152 says the loop "prefers the bulk variant when available" and line 248 requires placeholders to exercise both protocol paths. No adapter or dispatch is specified.
- **Data-flow step 4 describes the wrong model.** It describes the per-agent form, which is not what `tick()` takes.
- **`accelerations` is never used.** It is in `AgentState` (line 96) but no data-flow step reads or writes it, and the slice plan entry lists only positions, velocities and profile indices.

Fix: cut the per-agent `Force` protocol (or specify a single `per_agent_to_bulk` adapter as its only use), cut `accelerations`, and rewrite step 4 in bulk terms.

findings.title: SpatialQuery result contract is too loose for the determinism guarantee
findings.description:
The protocol does not say whether results include the querying agent, or in what order indices are returned. Both matter downstream:
- **Self-inclusion:** every force in 101–104 needs to know whether to exclude itself.
- **Ordering:** floating-point summation order follows neighbor order. Slice 105 must show "behavioral output is identical before and after the swap," and the architecture's Tick determinism goal depends on it.

Fix: state self-exclusion (or inclusion), ascending index order, and whether the boundary is `<=` or `<` radius.

findings.title: No environment input on tick or force protocols
findings.description:
The architecture's tick "receives the current agent state, environmental context, and an optional active-agent subset," and lists "Environment as input surface" as a principle. Neither `tick()` nor `BulkForce` carries environment context, while the slice promises that later slices use `tick()` as-is.

The slice plan does not assign environment to (100), so deferring is acceptable. One sentence should say how it arrives later, for example forces as callables that close over a read-only environment handle.

findings.title: Removal semantics and index stability are unspecified
findings.description: Remove "resizes arrays," but agents are identified only by array index. The caller owns `active_indices` across ticks, so removal silently invalidates caller-held indices. State whether removal compacts or swap-removes, and that indices are not stable identifiers.

findings.title: Invalid-input behavior for `tick()` is not stated
findings.description: The slice has no network or file I/O, so hang, timeout and disconnect modes do not apply. It does not say what happens for out-of-range or duplicate `active_indices`, out-of-range `profile_indices`, non-positive `dt`, or non-finite forces. The project's "fail explicitly" rule suggests a guard clause at the tick boundary.

findings.title: Integration section renders as a code block
findings.description: The "Integration: Semi-Implicit Euler" heading and body are indented four spaces, so Markdown renders them as preformatted text and the heading is lost.
